why: Every row here needs a human before it is shown to a student. Either the recomputed working contradicts the answer the paper marked, or the two independent readings of the green tick disagreed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question_en: The acceleration of a particle is increasing linearly with time t as 6t. The particle starts from the origin with an initial velocity 10 m/s. The distance travelled by the particle after 2 seconds will be
questions.note: Marked correct option (18 m) does not match recomputed physics: with a=6t and v0=10 m/s, x(t)=10t+t³ gives x(2)=28 m, not 18 m. The question text and the green-tick position were read clearly and are transcribed faithfully; flagging the mismatch for verification against the official key.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question_en: A metal cube absorbs 2100.0 J of heat when its temperature is raised by 2 °C. If the specific heat of the metal is 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, then the mass of the cube is
questions.note: Printed marked-correct value (1.116 kg) does not match Q=mcΔT computation (≈1.167 kg); transcribed exactly as printed and marked.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question_en: In a double-slit experiment performed in air the angular width of a fringe is found to be 0.15° on a screen placed 80 cm away. The wavelength of light used is 490 nm. The angular width of the fringe if the entire apparatus is immersed in a medium of refractive index 5/3 is
questions.note: marked correct option (0.9°) is inconsistent with the standard relation θ_medium = θ_air / n, which gives 0.09° (option 1); transcribed exactly as printed, flagging for review

questions.note: The paper's key marks option 3 ("6") as correct. Standard chemistry gives the number of nearest neighbours (coordination number) in a BCC unit cell as 8 (option 2), which contradicts the marked key. Recorded the marked option per instructions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question_en: Statement I: Specific resistance depends on nature of material and independent of temperature of the material. Statement II: A wire of resistance 6 Ω is drawn out so that its new length is four times its original length. The resistance of the new wire is 48 Ω. Statement III: Drift velocity is the average constant velocity acquired by free electrons inside a metal by the application of an electric field which results in current. Which of the following is correct?
options_en: Statements I, II and III are true
Statement I is true, but, Statements II, III is false
Statement III is true, but Statements I, II are false
Statements II, III are true but Statement I is false
questions.note: Adjudicated by hand against the image: this reading of the tick is wrong, the tick is on option 3.

questions.question_en: An alkene X (C₄H₈) exhibits geometrical isomerism. Oxidation of A with KMnO₄ | H⁺ gave Y. On heating sodium salt of Y with a mixture of NaOH and CaO gave Z. What is Z?
questions.note: Printed question contradicts itself: the alkene is named X, but the next sentence says "Oxidation of A with KMnO4 | H+ gave Y" — transcribed exactly as printed (A is never otherwise defined; presumed to mean X).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question_en: A conductor of length 1.5 m and area of cross-section 3×10⁻⁵ m² has electrical resistance of 15 Ω. The current density in the conductor for an electric field of 21 Vm⁻¹ is
questions.note: Green tick is clearly on option 2 (0.7×10⁻⁶ Am⁻²) in the source image, but computing J = σE with σ = L/(RA) = 1.5/(15×3×10⁻⁵) gives J = 0.7×10⁵ Am⁻² (option 4). Recorded exactly as marked; flagging possible answer-key error.
